lesson.menu_desc: Three songs, three moments: the music you have been listening to all your life, and what it is about each song that stays with you -- 13 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- The Soundtrack of My Life
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eglis Roberto | Lesson 8 -- The Soundtrack of My Life

listenings.text: I have been listening to the same bands since I was fifteen. My kids laugh at me, but I do not care. It was my older brother who gave me my first record, and I still have it. What I love about old songs is that they take me back. When I hear a certain tune, I am twenty again, on a beach in the summer, with my friends. These days, I have been listening to a lot of jazz in the car, and I have been trying to learn the piano for about a year. I am terrible, but I play every morning. For me, music is not new or old. It is a time machine.

My father always says that music was better in his time. Honestly, what I hate is when people stop looking for new music at forty. I am fifty-eight, and I have been discovering new artists every week for years. I follow young musicians from Brazil, from Nigeria, from Korea. Sometimes I do not understand the lyrics, but I understand the feeling. It was a song in Portuguese that made me want to visit Brazil, and I have been learning the language for two years now. Old music is beautiful, of course. But what keeps me young is the next song, not the last one.
